title: Centric's 200+ own software products make it a channel-conflict risk rather than a delivery partner
content:
The flag on Centric states the disqualifier in its own words: product IP is a channel-conflict risk. The tool field explains the scale of it — more than 200 of its own software products, plus Peppol — against verticals of public, retail, banking and industry, and a Dutch profile of insurance, public and retail.

The mechanism is straightforward and hard to work around. A partner that already sells its own product for a given process has a revenue line to protect, so placing a competing build in front of the same buyer costs it money. Channel conflict is not a matter of goodwill; with a portfolio that broad, the overlap with almost any candidate solution is close to certain.

Ownership churn compounds it. The firm was acquired by the Imker Capital consortium in July 2024, the flag says strategy is unsettled and the current structure needs verifying, and revenue is recorded at 425 million with no currency stated. On top of that the row is a provisional v2 tail entry, mechanically rescored on size and slot occupancy, with an OSS-portfolio screen still outstanding — so the one well-evidenced thing about Centric is the conflict.

Product IP is a channel-conflict risk.
description: The flag names the risk directly; revenue is recorded at 425 million and a Jul-2024 buyout by the Imker Capital consortium left strategy unsettled and the structure unverified.
